newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower with crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower with crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to lower Tuesday in sluggish trade, with low sulphurs pressured by relatively light utility demand and weaker crude and gas prices, industry sources said.
While some colder East Coast weather this week may boost heating loads, traders said it would take some sustained cold to trim ample inventories.
"We're finally getting some colder weather, but there's a lot of oil around," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped 50 cents to about $19.75 a barrel, traders said.

NYH January one percent paper sold early at $20.05 and $20.10 but slipped below $20 later, down more than a quarter. Feb paper traded as high as $20.40 early, then was quoted at about $19.75, off about 50 cents, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour eased slightly to $20.75-21.00 on reports of a HP sale late Monday at $20.70 and a HP tender award at about $21. The NYPA tender for 100,000 barrels of 0.3 HP for Jan 15 delivery was awarded at about $21, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York again were little changed.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $18.50-75 and three percent at $16.50.

New York city gate gas prices tacked on another 50 cents Tuesday to the $4.50/mmBtu area on expectations for colder East Coast weather this week. NYH one percent resid slipped to a $3.14/mmBtu equivalent.
